meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural): Quebec private law, including partnership law, follows the civil law tradition under the Civil Code of Québec; federal taxation, criminal law and AML/CFT statutes are common law based.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all general partners, limited partners and UBOs against Global Affairs Canada's Canadian Sanctions List; FINTRAC PEP and adverse-conduct indicators; OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists for USD-clearing AdMob/AppLovin payments; UNSC Consolidated List; and public enforcement/database checks including Interpol Red Notices. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any domestic or foreign PEP, criminal record, adverse media, high-risk jurisdiction or inconsistent source of wealth. Services are refused where any match survives verification. Ongoing re-screening is required at least every 90 days and upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec enterprise names must be entered in French. The mandatory legal designation for a limited partnership is 'société en commandite' or the initials 'S.E.C.'. The name must be distinctive, non-deceptive and not confusing with existing names in the Quebec register. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script; French accents and orthographic rules are enforced. A bilingual or English courtesy translation may be registered as a secondary name, but the French name is the legally operative name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused on distinctiveness, prohibited-token or confusing-grounds grounds, the applicant may request an informal review by Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days. The review submission must include the registraire's refusal letter, a revised name incorporating the French mandated 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' designation, a fresh name-search certificate, and any consent letters for sensitive tokens or evidence of goodwill. A name reservation may be extended if filed before expiry for the statutory extension period. After a final adverse decision, judicial review lies in the Superior Court of Québec under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible but conditional for a hyper-casual gaming LP: a commercial virtual office in Quebec may be used as the low-risk registered address for service, provided it is a physical street address staffed during business hours and service acceptance is contracted. Pure mail-forwarding without a local management or record-keeping arrangement will not satisfy Quebec enterprise registration substance expectations. For zero-license digital publishing, no dedicated premises are mandated, but CRA/Revenu Québec may examine whether the LP's 'place of management' creates a taxable establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: approximately 5% cumulative probability over the first 36 months for an unannounced physical inspection; probability increases to 15-20% upon filing of unusual GST/QST returns, continuing losses, related-party app store royalty transfers, or a foreign PEP being newly identified as an UBO.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2245 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 22, 31 and 34; Regulation respecting fees payable under the Act (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) – online portal www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca with counters in Québec City and Montréal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de société en commandite (Declaration of Limited Partnership) filed electronically; upon registration the Registrar issues an attested extract and the Québec enterprise number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account rule under Québec law (C.C.Q. arts. 2236–2245). The declaration must state the amount or value of each limited partner's contribution; a limited partner who participates in management forfeits limited-liability protection (art. 2238). Non-resident partners may contribute in any currency; the partnership issues units recorded in the partnership register rather than share capital. Low capitalization is acceptable for software publishing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the board of [GP Holdings Inc.], general partner of Hyper-Casual Quebec Games S.E.C. (the 'Partnership'): (1) the partnership agreement and declaration are approved, and subscription to partnership units by the general partner and each limited partner is authorized, with contributions as recorded in the declaration; (2) the registered office is established at [1230, rue de l'Écran, Ville de Québec] and management is directed to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Registraire des entreprises; (3) [Officer Name] is appointed Managing Director and [Officer Name] Secretary-Compliance Officer, with authority to open bank accounts and execute AdMob and AppLovin payout agreements; and (4) ancillary statutory filings are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the partnership name and verify prior-name claims
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name-reservation module (Services Québec).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a Central Registry search to ensure the proposed French-language name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entry; submit the name-reservation request and pay the fee. The reservation is valid for 90 days and must be referenced in the declaration; use a distinctive element plus 's.e.c.' or 'Limited Partnership' suffix.
required_dossiers: Name reservation form (formulaire de réservation de nom)
Written mandate of the general partner if filed by an agent
Proof of fee payment (CAD 35)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, choose one of the alternative names proposed by the examiner within 30 days or file a written factual rebuttal; a consent letter from the prior registrant may overcome an identical or confusingly similar prior name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the declaration of limited partnership and partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel or notary (no government pre-clearance); the executed declaration is later filed with the Registraire des entreprises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the signed declaration containing the partnership name, object (publishing of lightweight ad-monetized mobile games), head-office address in Québec, and the name and contribution of each limited partner. Identify the general partner and, if it is a corporation, prove solvency and board authority. All partners execute the declaration and the internal partnership agreement; non-resident limited partners are admitted with pass-through tax treatment noted.
required_dossiers: Draft declaration of limited partnership
Limited partnership agreement (signed by GP and LPs)
GP board resolution authorizing execution
Identity documents and registry extract for GP; passport/address proof for LPs
Proof of registered office address (lease or attestation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the document is materially defective, prepare an amending declaration and obtain fresh signatures; no notarization is mandatory unless real property is contributed, in which case a notarial deed and publication are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the declaration and obtain the enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – electronic filing portal (Inscription d'une société en commandite).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed declaration, pay the registration fee, and submit. The Registrar issues the dated attestation and the NEQ. The partnership exists from registration with a distinct patrimony; only persons authorized by the declaration may bind it, and the general partner is the registered administrator for third parties.
required_dossiers: Signed declaration of limited partnership (electronic)
Name-reservation certificate
Certificate of status of the GP from the Québec registry
List of partners and contribution values
Payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, furnish the requested clarifications or corrected signatures within 30 days; use the correction module (déclaration modificative) or request administrative review of a refusal within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for federal and Québec tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online – partnership account 'RP') and Revenu Québec (QST/GST registration module).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate a federal partnership account for GST/HST and T5013 filings using the general partner's business number, and register the partnership for QST with Revenu Québec when taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000 per year. Apply the place-of-supply rules to AdMob/AppLovin digital-advertising revenues and maintain partner allocation schedules for non-resident limited partners.
required_dossiers: Attested extract of the LP (NEQ)
GP's registration and certificate of status
Partnership declaration and agreement
List of partners for T5013 allocation
Non-resident partner information for Part XIII/s. 116 purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec misclassifies the account as a corporation, call the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525) or use the Revenu Québec correction request to change the account type; eligible late-registration penalties can be reduced under voluntary disclosure before CRA contact.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt statutory governance records and open commercial bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner's board of directors, with the banking counterparty (Schedule I bank) completing KYC at the Québec registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the GP board and approve the first board resolution; adopt a minute book containing the partnership agreement, declaration, GP resolution, partner register and signatory mandate. Open CAD and USD accounts for AdMob/AppLovin disbursements and complete beneficial-ownership attestation for partners holding more than 25%. Designate a person responsible for Québec Law 25 privacy compliance and gaming-data processing protocols.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Attested LP extract and GP certificate of good standing
Partnership agreement and partner register
Bank KYC forms and signatory mandate
Québec Law 25 privacy and data-processing statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML/KYC information, provide the Low-Risk_Standard classification rationale and a legal opinion confirming the LP's existence and the GP's authority; escalate to the bank's compliance department if conditions imposed exceed the demonstrated risk profile.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 5820 (software publishing) is office-based. If a physical office is leased, the local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal Service des permis et inspections) grants the commercial-occupancy permit, and the city may impose a business tax (taxe d'affaires).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is required for hyper-casual game publishing in Québec; the mandatory registrations are the Registraire des entreprises registration (NEQ), GST/HST and QST accounts, and, if user data is processed, a Privacy Officer designation under Québec Law 25 (CQLR c P-39.1).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 'Nil') – office-based game publishing generates no effluent discharge, no atmospheric emissions and no hazardous waste; only standard office e-waste recycling and municipal waste bylaws apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital product itself. If the company internally hosts servers, MELCCFP greenhouse-gas reporting thresholds (25,000 tCO2e/year under CQLR c Q-2, s. 46.1) would apply; otherwise comply with municipal wastewater, electrical-waste and recycling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety or structural certification for a virtual head office. If physical premises are leased, obtain a municipal fire-safety certificate under the Québec Safety Code, comply with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1) and CNESST workplace first-aid rules, and meet building and accessibility codes for the leased occupancy class.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - GST/HST Registration Portal and Business Number (BN) account; Revenu Québec - Québec Sales Tax (QST) registration and Registre des entreprises (NEQ) portal for the Province of Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or foreign-owned limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec must first obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) through Revenu Québec's Registre des entreprises, then register for a CRA Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST account using Form RC348 or the CRA's Business Registration Online service, followed by a separate QST registration through Revenu Québec using Form LM-1-V. The general partner (or its authorized representative) must hold legal authority to bind the partnership. The partnership itself is the registrant for GST/HST and QST; the general partner is jointly and severally liable for the partnership's obligations. Proof of foreign existence, registered address in Quebec, and a Quebec agent for service may be required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime comparable to the U.S. IRS § 7701. A Canadian limited partnership is by default a fiscally transparent partnership for Canadian income tax purposes, with income, gains, and losses allocated to partners. No elective entity-level taxation is available to a Quebec limited partnership. However, for GST/HST and QST, a partnership is treated as a person and may elect under the Excise Tax Act and QST legislation to have certain closely related corporations or partnership members report and remit tax; selected listed financial institution rules and partnership anti-avoidance allocations must be reviewed. A hybrid mismatch election is not statutorily available; taxpayers must rely on Canadian domestic law and the Canada-U.S. treaty applicable provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: A person or partnership becomes a registrant for GST/HST and QST once its worldwide taxable revenues from taxable supplies made in Canada and Quebec, including through permanent establishments, exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. For a non-resident partnership whose only taxable supplies are zero-rated exports, registration is generally not compulsory but may be elected voluntarily to claim input tax refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscally cleared electronic invoicing or a central government clearance platform for GST/HST or QST. Electronic invoices are acceptable if the invoicing system produces a complete, legible, and verifiable record of supplier and customer information, tax amounts, dates, and tax numbers. Quebec however imposes a regulated electronic billing and payment infrastructure for certain business-to-business transactions through Revenu Québec, but this does not require cryptographic fiscal stamps. Taxpayers using software must ensure audit trail integrity and meet record-keeping obligations under the Excise Tax Act and the QST Act. For hyper-casual gaming revenue, the supply is generally an electronically supplied service; no customs-style clearance applies, but books and records must demonstrate the place of supply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada (including Quebec) by the registrant and to certain services performed for non-residents. For digital hyper-casual mobile gaming services, the supply is zero-rated as a supply made to a non-resident person where the recipient is outside Canada and no Canadian payment/collection nexus triggers taxation. Ad-mediation and platform payouts from AdMob and AppLovin do not themselves create a deemed supply in Canada; the app developer must evidence that the end-user downloading and gameplay occurs outside Quebec/Canada. Where a non-resident platform sells the game to Canadian consumers, the game publisher may be deemed to be carrying on business through a Quebec permanent establishment if the place of management or road-warrior activities are in Canada. Zero-rating of exported goods additionally requires proof of export within a reasonable time (generally 60 days) and possession of prescribed export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13 or equivalent electronic export reporting)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or other carrier transport document evidencing delivery to a foreign destination
Cargo Control / Freight Waybill documentation demonstrating the goods left Canada in the same or substantially unchanged state
Foreign customs entry or proof of importation in the destination country, when available
Commercial invoice and contract of sale showing the foreign buyer and sale price
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice confirming foreign currency payment (/foreign exchange repatriation ledger)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated returns and claw back input tax credits together with interest and penalties if the exporter fails to substantiate that the supply was exported or supplied to a non-resident. Penalties for knowingly making a false statement in a GST/HST or QST return are the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax amount, plus provincial penalties under the QST regime. Habitual disregard or fraudulent zero-rating claims may lead to criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act, criminal interest, and disgorgement of refunds. For digital services, the CRA uses taxpayer portal data, payment rails (AdMob/AppLovin payout records), and platform geographic metadata to challenge unfounded zero ratings. The exporter must retain electronic evidence of IP address geolocation by installed user base, platform reporting, bank wire/remittance records, and contracts with advertising networks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); administered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF enforcement, while the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises all federally incorporated banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility under IMF Article VIII and imposes no exchange controls or capital account restrictions. The Canadian dollar is freely floating and fully convertible for both current and capital transactions. A Quebec limited partnership may remit profits and returns of capital to non-resident partners without exchange-control approval; the only fiscal impediment is the non-resident Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, typically 25% unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty. US-dollar receipts from AdMob, AppLovin and other ad networks may be retained in USD bank accounts in Canada or transferred abroad without mandatory conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has no statutory obligation requiring exporters to surrender, convert or repatriate export proceeds, and there is no prescribed timeline or conversion ratio for holding foreign currency receipts. The only FIAR-relevant requirement is that physical cross-border movement of monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and FINTRAC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD) and Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
USD Clearing Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex may be used as payment facilitators for low-value operational flows, but they cannot replace a Canadian Schedule I bank for capital escrow, profit distribution, or statutory corporate treasury accounts. Any EMI operating in Canada must register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, in Quebec, obtain a money-services business permit from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Non-registered offshore EMIs will be rejected by Canadian compliance as non-compliant deposit takers. If properly registered, EMIs are acceptable only for outgoing micro-payouts and developer settlements, not for capital injections or partner distributions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Federal law does not impose a blanket in-person appearance requirement, but compliance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) mandates reliable identity verification of every limited partner, the general partner, directors, and authorized signatories. In practice, most Quebec Tier-1 banks require an in-person or high-confidence live video interview with the general partner and signing officers. Remote account opening is feasible for a domestically registered limited partnership provided all corporate records are notarized, an AML questionnaire is completed, and the bank accepts a virtual KYC process. For foreign-based general partners, a physical meeting at a Canadian branch or at the office of retained Canadian counsel is usually mandated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure typical of a limited partnership with multiple passive limited partners and a foreign corporate general partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement, Certificate of Declaration of Registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, detailed beneficial ownership schedule listing each partner's full legal name, date of birth, citizenship, residential address, tax residence and ownership percentage, an organizational chart, passport copies, and proof of residential address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value digital payouts from US ad networks (AdMob and AppLovin) resembling micro-transactions or possible gaming-money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements and payout terms with Google AdMob and AppLovin, platform earnings reports, monthly bank statements and settlement reconciliations, user-acquisition and cash-flow forecasts, business plan, source-of-funds declaration, and the company's internal AML/CTF risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD capital flows involving non-resident partners without an immediately evident commercial or economic purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds documentation for each capital contribution (bank statements, share-sale certificates, executed loan agreements, tax returns), a completed FINTRAC-compliant AML/KYC questionnaire, confirmation of each partner's tax residence, audited or management-prepared financial statements, a legal opinion on Part XIII withholding obligations, and evidence that the allocation of taxable Canadian income is transparent and documented.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be sent via SWIFT MT103 with the exact beneficiary legal name matching the limited partnership's bank account. The remitter should include a purpose code and field 70 narrative such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO CANADIAN LIMITED PARTNERSHIP'. For USD payments, use the Canadian bank's US correspondent clearing chain (e.g., JPMorgan Chase or Citibank); for CAD, use wire routing through SWIFT or the recipient bank's direct clearing. FINTRAC and the receiving institution may request a source-of-funds package for any wire exceeding CAD 10,000. All inbound wires should be pre-advised to the relationship manager with supporting partnership documentation to avoid hold-ups.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements to game developers, advertising networks, and international vendors should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for intercountry USD/CAD wires; for Canadian domestic payments, use the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or regular bank wire. Commercial letters of credit (UCP600) remain permissible but are rarely suitable for intangible digital services; a standby letter of credit may be issued to secure material advance payments if contractually required. The partnership may maintain a USD-denominated account to minimize FX conversion costs and to streamline payments to US-based ad networks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward contracts (CAD/USD) with a Canadian Schedule I bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for emerging-market currency exposures if the partnership later expands to jurisdictions with illiquid or non-convertible currencies
Standard spot transactions for immediate settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (LPED, CQLR c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the last day of the month following the anniversary month of initial registration (i.e., within one calendar month after the registration anniversary date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing is subject to administrative monetary penalties per LPED; continued non-filing for 10 consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off or cancellation of the registration by the Registrar, resulting in loss of legal publicity and inability to enforce rights in Quebec.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec law does not mandate audit for a limited partnership unless it qualifies as a 'large enterprise' — i.e., gross revenue exceeding CAD 10 million AND total assets exceeding CAD 10 million — in which case audited financial statements must be filed with the Registrar; a corporate-style audit obligation under the QBCA applies only if the entity were incorporated with 10 or more shareholders and assets above CAD 10 million or revenue above CAD 20 million, which is inapplicable to an LP as structured.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); an unlisted Quebec limited partnership may elect either framework consistently; fiscal and tax reporting to Revenu Québec must reconcile to the chosen framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under LPED, every registered enterprise must identify its ultimate beneficiaries in the enterprise registry; the annual declaration serves as the mandatory annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial owner data, and any change in ownership or control occurring during the year must be disclosed to the Registrar within 15 days of the change to maintain registry accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Limited Partners and General Partner)
Register of Directors of the General Partner (if applicable)
Minute Book of the Partnership and General Partner
Register of Capital Contributions (shares of profits and losses)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – 1,300 per annum for a professional registered office and agent-for-service arrangement in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 22,000 per annum if a full financial statement audit is voluntarily obtained; generally avoidable below the statutory large-enterprise threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal + Quebec general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). The Quebec Limited Partnership (LP) is fiscally transparent; no entity-level income tax is imposed and the rate applies at the partner level when a corporate partner is taxed on its share of LP income. For active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner up to CAD 500,000, the combined small business rate is 12.2% (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in Canada or Quebec. Preferential measures: (i) Quebec Interactive Digital Media / Video Game Tax Credit of 30% of eligible Quebec labour expenditures, increased to 37.5% for production facilities located outside the Communautés métropolitaines de Montréal and de Québec (refundable subject to rules and reduced by any federal ITC); (ii) federal SR&ED investment tax credit: 35% fully refundable for CCPCs on qualified expenditures up to the expenditure limit, otherwise 15% non-refundable; (iii) Quebec SR&ED credit of 14% for CCPCs on the first CAD 3,000,000 of eligible expenditures (30% credit for certain CSEs; non-refundable for larger corporations). Credits flow through the LP to its partners in accordance with each partner's share.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Summary and T5013 slips (Partnership Information Return) filed electronically through the CRA's 'Internet File Transfer' or approved EFILE software (e-Partnership). Triggering conditions for filing include the LP having a non-resident partner, a corporate or partnership member, six or more members, or a permanent establishment outside Canada.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 is due on or before the day that is 5 months after the end of the LP's fiscal period (e.g., 31 May following a 31 December year-end). Each corporate partner files its own T2 return within 2 months (non-CCPC) or 3 months (CCPC) of the partner's year-end; individual partners file T1 by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Limited partner's share of limited partnership business income (or loss). This is the primary flow-through allocation for the hyper-casual games operating results, net of deductible costs (UA spend, platform fees, salaries, amortization of intangible assets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for each non-resident limited partner. The CRA is notified of the allocation; no Part XIII withholding is applied at the partnership level on the allocated business income itself. The non-resident partner must file a Canadian Part I tax return (T1 or T2) to settle federal and Quebec tax and must claim any treaty relief on that return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General partner's share of partnership business income (or loss). Reported for the managing/general partner, typically the Canadian holding corporation of the game studio group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner is a non-resident, the same Part I filing obligation applies and the general partner's share is taxable in Canada as business income carried on through a permanent establishment. Treaty protection (e.g., Canada-US Article VII) applies only where no permanent establishment exists, which is factually difficult for a managing general partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership fiscal period-end date (YYYY/MM/DD). Establishes the 5-month statutory due date for the T5013 and the taxable year in which each partner reports its share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident partner must align the Canadian reporting of its share with the LP fiscal year-end; specified foreign reporting rules (Form T1134 for a foreign affiliate, if any) run independently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income and other deductions: e.g., interest income, foreign exchange gains, IP royalties earned by the LP from sub-licensing game code, platform bonuses, and deductions for professional fees and software licences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income traceable to Canadian-source IP royalties paid by the LP to a non-resident licensor is separately caught under Part XIII. The non-resident partner's share of these other amounts is reported on the T5013 and the partner must file a Part I return; treaty reduced rates do not apply to business income without a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) for income tax purposes of the partnership: reconciles the sum of all partners' shares to the partnership's audited financial results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident partner's share must equal the proportion of the LP agreement's agreed allocation; a departure from the profit-sharing ratio attracts audit scrutiny and may trigger the sham doctrine.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: failure to file the T5013 is penalized at CAD 25 per partner per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); where the return is more than 24 months late, the penalty rises to CAD 100 per partner per day (maximum CAD 25,000) (ITA s. 162(3)). Partners who omit a share of income face the 10% repeated-failure penalty (ITA s. 163(1)) and the 50% gross-negligence penalty (ITA s. 163(2)), plus interest on arrears.
